validity.recommendation: Keep as a distinct row (not a duplicate). Retitle/describe as the GASCO 'Abr Sinai' domestic trans-Sinai trunk (Port Said/El Tina area -> El Arish), correctly classed gas transmission.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE and CLASSIFICATION: real, correctly classified. Independent EIB (European Investment Bank) EIA package for 'GASCO Abr Sinai/Abr Seina Onshore Gas Pipeline' (Egyptian Natural Gas Co., Nov 2007, consultant PETROSAFE) documents an EXISTING 32-inch, 111 km pipeline running El-Tina Sharkiya/El-Tena East (east bank of the Suez Canal, Port Said governorate) -> Roman compressor station -> Bir El-Abd -> El Arish, Northern Sinai, plus a 2007 duplication project adding a parallel 36-inch, 111 km line on the same route 'to increase gas manoeuvring along Sinai... and transport gas from El-Tena East to El-Areish Industrial area.' A 2011 Arabic news source (youm7, already in the sheet as the current FuelSource value) independently corroborates the corridor's western end, describing the AGP/Sinai gas route as starting 'from the El-Gamil area in Port Said governorate... running about 41 km, then passing under the Suez Canal into Sinai.' GulfPub PE World Map (Tier-2, SDE Dec-2025 scrape) independently lists a matching entry 'Port Said - El Arish Pipeline' (operating, operator=EGAS, diameter=36in) -- strong name/endpoint/diameter match confirming this is a real, currently-tracked pipeline, not a phantom. CLASSIFICATION: this is a proper inter-regional gas transmission trunk (feeds Sinai's domestic grid and the Arish origination point of the Arab Gas Pipeline / EMG interconnection), not a gathering or plant-internal line. DUPLICATE CHECK against the 30-pipeline Egypt gas-operating roster: NOT a duplicate of P0436 (Arab Gas Pipeline, Arish->South Sinai/Taba, which continues FROM Arish onward toward Aqaba -- opposite direction, different corridor) nor P0462 (Arish-Ashkelon Pipeline, the Israeli subsea EMG import line, Ashkelon->North Sinai -- different route entirely, landing near but not the same infrastructure). P3659 is the distinct westbound domestic feeder from the Port Said/Suez Canal side into Arish. No duplicate found. Confidence tier: medium (one authoritative single-origin EIA document + one independent Tier-2 dataset match + one independent-but-weaker Arabic news corroboration on the western segment).

validity.recommendation: Re-derive Length. No independent source supports 235 km for a single route. Best independent estimate is ~147-152 km (GulfPub's independent 'Port Said - El Arish Pipeline' = 147 km; EIB EIA's sourced single-line El-Tena East->El-Arish segment = 111 km, plus youm7's ~41 km El Gamil->Suez-Canal-crossing segment upstream of it, sums to ~152 km). 235 km does not match either figure and does not cleanly match summing the two 2007-era parallel 32in+36in loops (111+111=222) either. Flag for human resolution before trusting the current value.
validity.researcher_notes: SPEC check on Length: current GEM value is 235.00 km (unreferenced). Two independent sources converge on a materially shorter route: (1) GulfPub PE World Map (Tier-2) lists the matching 'Port Said - El Arish Pipeline' at 147 km; (2) the EIB EIA package gives an explicit, coordinate-anchored 111 km for the El-Tena East (Suez Canal east bank, Port Said governorate) -> Roman -> Bir El-Abd -> El Arish segment, and the 2011 youm7 article separately describes an upstream ~41 km segment from El-Gamil (Port Said) to the Suez Canal crossing point that feeds into that same corridor -- summing to ~152 km, i.e. essentially the same figure GulfPub gives independently. No source found supports anything near 235 km. A plausible (but unconfirmed) origin of the 235 km figure is double-counting the 2007 'duplication' project, which added a second parallel 36in 111 km line alongside the original 32in 111 km line on the same corridor (111+111=222, still short of 235, and would double-count pipe rather than measure route length per GEM convention). Recommend the researcher/human editor re-derive Length from GulfPub's 147 km or the EIB-sourced ~152 km corridor total, not carry the current 235 km forward without support.

validity.recommendation: Drop the 42in component or re-verify it against a primary source. Independent sourcing supports a 32in (original, pre-2007) + 36in (2007 duplicate) parallel-pipe pair on this corridor, not '36, 42'.
validity.researcher_notes: SPEC check on Diameter: current GEM value is '36, 42' in (dual-valued). The EIB EIA package -- the only source found with primary diameter data for this exact corridor -- describes the ORIGINAL existing pipeline as 32in and the 2007 duplication as 36in, both 111 km, El-Tena East->El-Arish. GulfPub independently corroborates the 36in figure ('Port Said - El Arish Pipeline', dia=36) but does not mention a second diameter. No source found (EIB, GulfPub, youm7, or general web search) supports a 42in component anywhere on this corridor. This looks like it may be a data-entry error (e.g. confusion with the nearby El Gamil-Damietta Gas Pipeline, GEM ProjectID P6037, which IS 42in but runs El Gamil->Damietta, a different destination) rather than a genuine attribute of this pipeline. Recommend the diameter be corrected to '36, 32' pending a primary-source check, not left as '36, 42'.

routes.corridor_desc: El Gamil (Port Said governorate, Mediterranean coast) -> ~41 km inland/south to a crossing beneath the Suez Canal near El-Tina Sharkiya/El-Qantara East (per youm7, 2011) -> the GASCO 'Abr Sinai' onshore corridor runs east-southeast through North Sinai via Roman compressor station and Bir El-Abd -> El Arish (per EIB EIA, 2007, which gives explicit coordinates for the El-Tena East start point, Roman station, Bir El-Abd, and the El Arish end point of its 111 km El-Tena East->El-Arish segment). NOTE on the coordinates: the EIB document's own 'long.'/'lat.' labels appear transposed relative to actual geography (values it labels 'long.' fall in the 31-degree range typical of Sinai latitudes, and values it labels 'lat.' fall in the 32-34-degree range typical of Sinai longitudes); I have swapped them below to match known town locations (El Qantara East ~30.9N/32.3E, Bir el-Abd town ~31.0N/33.0E, El Arish city ~31.13N/33.80E all land within a few km of the corrected points), and flag this transposition explicitly rather than silently using the document's literal labels.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoint city coordinates for El Gamil (a documented named landmark/former airfield in Port Said governorate) and El Arish are general-area, publicly known town/landmark coordinates, not tied to an exact valve-room location -- used only because no single source gives a precise El Gamil interconnection point. The three intermediate waypoints ARE tied to specific named GASCO facilities with EIB-sourced coordinates (with the lat/lon transposition correction noted above). No coordinate here was invented: every point is either a defensible named-place location or a corrected transcription of a primary-source coordinate. Given the transposition issue and the fact that the El Gamil->Suez-Canal segment relies on a single weaker (Arabic news, no coordinates) source, I recommend 'medium' rather than the current 'high' RouteAccuracy pending a cleaner primary source for the El Gamil segment specifically.

summary: P3659 is a real, correctly-classified pipeline (independently corroborated by EIB EIA docs + GulfPub as the GASCO 'Abr Sinai' Port Said-area-to-Arish trunk) and not a duplicate of P0436/P0462, but Length (235 km) and the '42in' diameter component are unsupported by any independent source (best estimate ~147-152 km, 32/36in not 36/42in), and the FuelSource cell contains a misplaced ref URL instead of a value -- all staged as concerns, nothing UNRESOLVED left blank without explanation.
